🔥🇲🇽 "Thirty-six years of governments for the rich. Three stolen elections. Then 2018." "The fraud of '88, when Cárdenas should have been president. 2006, when López Obrador should have been president. 2012, the vote-buying across the whole country. That was neoliberalism. And in 2018, the people of Mexico said: enough." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Santo Domingo Tonalá, Oaxaca Sheinbaum laid out the Plan Lázaro Cárdenas for the Mixteca — roads, water, schools, health clinics, artisan support — named for the general who spent his final years building dams, bridges, and roads in this region.

🇲🇽🚆 1,137 km of Mixteca roads — the size of Mexico City's entire primary road network. "What we're intervening in the Mixteca is 1,137 kilometers. To put it in perspective: Mexico City's primary road network — Periférico, Circuito Interior, the Ejes Viales — is 1,100 kilometers. That is the equivalent of what we are doing here." — Jesús Esteva, Infrastructure Secretary, Santo Domingo Tonalá 4.9 billion pesos for Mixteca roads; 37.8 billion for Oaxaca in 2026. 20 asphalt plants running, 20 work fronts simultaneously, 24 bridges underway, 92 hand-built community roads with indigenous assemblies.

🇲🇽🌎 "I will never accept a foreign government on our territory." "Maximilian told Juárez: 'Join my government.' Juárez answered: 'I will never accept a foreign government on our territory.' And the Second Independence triumphed — thanks to Juárez, the Mexican liberals, and the people of Mexico who fought for their sovereignty." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Santo Domingo Tonalá, Oaxaca Speaking in the heart of the Mixteca, Sheinbaum traced the three great presidents formed in Oaxaca — Juárez, Cárdenas, López Obrador — and closed: "In Mexico we will never put our independence at risk."
banner: "NEVER A FOREIGN GOVERNMENT ON OUR SOIL"

text: 🇲🇽✊ 12 million families. One in three Mexican households. "In the past, governments ruled for a few. Now we are governments of the people, by the people, and for the people of Mexico. That is the big difference." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Huajuapan, Oaxaca The Vivienda para el Bienestar program: 1.8M new homes, 1.8M improvement credits, 1M property titles, 5.2M restructured mortgages, 2.2M Infonavit credits. In Huajuapan, the first 68 of 412 homes were delivered today — at half their commercial value.

🇲🇽✊ Infonavit's housing fund: 140 billion pesos in 2018. 1.08 trillion today. "That money used to finance soda factories, beer companies, the mining industry, the European space program — a thousand things, except housing. The President instructed us: this money is for building homes, because the country needs them badly." — Octavio Romero Oropeza, Infonavit Director, Huajuapan, Oaxaca The minimum wage rose from 80 to 248 pesos/day under AMLO, then +12% and +13% under Sheinbaum — and workers' 5% housing contributions multiplied the fund eightfold. Infonavit has placed 32,000+ homes; 516,000 are approved or under contract, 43% of the six-year goal.

🇲🇽✊ "How much does he owe now? Zero." "Félix Delfino borrowed 150,000 pesos. He had already paid 400,000 — and still owed 1.1 million. How much does he owe now? Zero. It's only justice: he had already paid more than double what he borrowed." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Vivienda para el Bienestar, Huajuapan, Oaxaca All 4.86 million "unpayable" Infonavit and FOVISSSTE mortgages were restructured by December 31, 2025. Over 400,000 families kept their homes outright. In Oaxaca, 22,600+ people are also getting their mortgage-release paperwork done free of charge.
banner: "HOW MUCH DOES HE OWE NOW? ZERO."
